To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcriptome sequences of two buckwheat species, Fagopryrum esculentu and Fagopyrum tataricum, were obtained using the 454 sequencing technology and that the resulting data were used in comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses.

the 454 transcriptome sequencing is a promising approach for de novo transcriptome sequencing of plants, that the resulting contigs can be used for phylogenetics, and that comparative transcriptome analysis of two congeneric plant species revealed genes that are differentially expressed in the flowers and inflorensces.

(a) the transcriptomes of the two species are largely similar but also differ in the expression of several hundred genes, and (b) phylogenetic analysis of 13 single-copy genes supports the monophyly of the Caryophylalles and asterids, and the sister relationship of the latter and the rosids.

the development of new resources that can be used for further functional studies of Fagopyrum and other plant taxa.
two aspects: first, we provide the first large-scale transcriptome sequence data for Fagopyrum, a group of plants that has been largely ignored by the genomics research.

the data presented here represent a significant contribution to the knowledge of the transcriptomes of two plant species and will serve as a valuable resource for future research on these and related species.
the 454 sequencing technology is suitable for the transcriptome analysis of non-model organisms, but the de novo assembly is not as efficient as in the case of model organisms.

we have obtained a set of expressed sequence tags for two species of Fagopyrum that can be used to facilitate the identification of genes involved in the biosynthesis of buckwheat seed storage proteins and other economically important traits.
the data generated will be useful in future research on Fagopyrum and other members of the order Caryophylalles.

the transcriptome data obtained here can be used to identify genes that are differentially expressed in the flowers of these two species and that the data can also serve as a basis for future studies on the evolution of these two species.

the data generated in this study can be used as a resource for future studies of Fagopyrum evolution, physiology, and development.
